questions.q: Of what will the psalmist sing forever?
questions.a: He will sing about how faithfully Yahweh has loved his people as he promised.

questions.q: What will the psalmist make known to future generations?
questions.a: He will tell future generations that Yahweh always does what he promises.

questions.q: How has Yahweh’s faithfulness been established?
questions.a: The fact that Yahweh is faithful to his people is as permanent as the heavens.

questions.q: With whom has a covenant been made?
questions.a: Yahweh has made a covenant and a solemn promise with David, the man he chose to be king of Israel.

questions.q: How long will David’s descendants rule as kings?
questions.a: Yahweh promised that David’s descendants would always rule as kings.

questions.q: What will the angels in heaven be praising Yahweh about?
questions.a: The angels in heaven will praise Yahweh for the wonderful things he does and celebrate how he always does what he promises.

questions.q: How do the council of holy ones treat God?
questions.a: When the holy beings gather together, they all treat God with respect and honor.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s faithfulness?
questions.a: Yahweh is always faithful in every way.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s rule of the sea?
questions.a: He says that Yahweh calms the waves of the sea so it will not become too violent.

questions.q: What did Yahweh use to scatter and defeat his enemies?
questions.a: He used his great power.

questions.q: What belongs to Yahweh who made the world and all it contains?
questions.a: The heavens and the earth belong to Yahweh who created the world and everything in it.

questions.q: What did Yahweh create?
questions.a: Yahweh created the full extent of the world in every direction.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about Yahweh using the images of his arm and hand?
questions.a: Yahweh is very powerful and uses his power to do great things.

questions.q: How does Yahweh rule?
questions.a: Yahweh always does what is right and just and is faithful and true in everything he does.

questions.q: What happens to the people who worship Yahweh?
questions.a: They are have truly good lives in which they enjoy Yahweh’s favor, and they rejoice in who Yahweh is and how he always does what is right.

questions.q: What did Yahweh give the people because of his favor?
questions.a: Because Yahweh was pleased with his people, made them strong and glorious and gave them a good king.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say belongs to Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel?
questions.a: The people’s king is the one who protects them and he belongs to Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say in a vision to his faithful ones?
questions.a: He said that he had given strength to a mighty warrior from among the people and had chosen him to be their king.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he will do for his chosen king David?
questions.a: He said he had anointed him, will support him, strengthen him, and defeat his enemies.

questions.q: How does Yahweh promise he will treat David?
questions.a: Yahweh will always be faithful to David and treat him kindly, and by Yahweh’s authority, make him a great ruler.

questions.q: What will David call out to Yahweh?
questions.a: He will call out to Yahweh as his Father, his God, and the one who protects and saves him.

questions.q: How will Yahweh treat David?
questions.a: He will treat him as if he were his firstborn son and make him the greatest of all kings on the earth.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for David?
questions.a: Yahweh will always love David faithfully always honor his covenant with him.

questions.q: How long will David’s descendants rule and his throne last?
questions.a: His descendants will always rule as kings and his dynasty will last as long as the skies exist.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to David’s descendants if they disobey Yahweh’s rules?
questions.a: Yahweh will punish them to correct them because of the wrong things they have done.

questions.q: What promises does Yahweh make to David even if the people disobey his rules?
questions.a: Yahweh promises not to stop faithfully loving David and doing what he promised for his descendants. He will not break his covenant or take back what he said.

questions.q: By what does Yahweh swear once and for all that he will keep these promises to David?
questions.a: Yahweh swears by his own holy character that he guarantees his promise to David.

questions.q: What does the psalmist now say about how the anointed one is being treated by Yahweh?
questions.a: The psalmist says that it appears that Yahweh has rejected the anointed king and has abandoned him.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say is happening to the people of Israel as represented by their king?
questions.a: Their city is being plundered by people who to steal from the city and the people of Israel are being ridiculed by the people around them.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say Yahweh has done regarding the enemies of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh has allowed their enemies to become strong and celebrate how they have defeated the people of Israel.

questions.q: What happened when the Israelites went into battle?
questions.a: Their armies have had to retreat from battles because Yahweh had not helped them.

questions.q: What has happened to the kingdom of Israel?
questions.a: The kingdom is no longer glorious and they no longer have a king.

questions.q: What has happened to Israel?
questions.a: They are no longer a strong nation as they had been and are completely disgraced.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about Yahweh and his anger?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to come to help them and not be angry with them any more.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to remember?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to remember how short life is and that he created all people as mere mortals.

questions.q: What does the psalmist remind the Lord about his promises?
questions.a: The psalmist reminds the Lord that he promised David that he would faithfully love his people.

questions.q: What else does the psalmist ask the Lord to remember?
questions.a: He asks the Lord to remember the insulting things people are saying about his people and how Yahweh’s enemies have been mocking the actions of his anointed king.

questions.q: How long does the psalmist say Yahweh will be blessed?
questions.a: Yahweh will be blessed forever.

commentary.text: God's mercy and truth, and his covenant.
The glory and perfection of God.
The happiness of those in communion with him.
God's covenant with David, as a type of Christ.
A calamitous state lamented, Prayer for redress.

Verses 1–4 Though our expectations may be disappointed, yet God's promises are established in the heavens, in his eternal counsels; they are out of the reach of opposers in hell and earth. And faith in the boundless mercy and everlasting truth of God, may bring comfort even in the deepest trials.

The more God's works are known, the more they are admired. And to praise the Lord, is to acknowledge him to be such a one that there is none like him. Surely then we should feel and express reverence when we worship God. But how little of this appears in our congregations, and how much cause have we to humble ourselves on this account! That almighty power which smote Egypt, will scatter the enemies of the church, while all who trust in God's mercy will rejoice in his name; for mercy and truth direct all he does. His counsels from eternity, and their consequences to eternity, are all justice and judgment.

Happy are those who so know the joyful sound of the gospel as to obey it; who experience its power upon their hearts, and bring forth the fruit of it in their lives. Though believers are nothing in themselves, yet having all in Christ Jesus, they may rejoice in his name. May the Lord enable us to do so. The joy of the Lord is the strength of his people; whereas unbelief dispirits ourselves and discourages others. Though it steals upon us under a semblance of humility, yet it is the very essence of pride. Christ is the Holy One of Israel; and in him was that peculiar people more blessed than in any other blessing.

The Lord anointed David with the holy oil, not only as an emblem of the graces and gifts he received, but as a type of Christ, the King Priest, and Prophet, anointed with the Holy Ghost without measure. David after his anointing, was persecuted, but none could gain advantage against him. Yet all this was a faint shadow of the Redeemer's sufferings, deliverance, glory, and authority, in whom alone these predictions and promises are fully brought to pass. He is the mighty God. This is the Redeemer appointed for us, who alone is able to complete the work of our salvation. Let us seek an interest in these blessings, by the witness of the Holy Spirit in our hearts. As the Lord corrected the posterity of David for their transgressions, so his people shall be corrected for their sins. Yet it is but a rod, not a sword; it is to correct, not to destroy. It is a rod in the hand of God, who is wise, and knows what he does; gracious, and will do what is best. It is a rod which they shall never feel, but when there is need. As the sun and moon remain in heaven, whatever changes there seem to be in them, and again appear in due season; so the covenant of grace made in Christ, whatever alteration seems to come to it, should not be questioned.

Sometimes it is not easy to reconcile God's providences with his promises, yet we are sure that God's works fulfil his word. When the great Anointed One, Christ himself, was upon the cross, God seemed to have cast him off, yet did not make void his covenant, for that was established for ever. The honour of the house of David was lost. Thrones and crowns are often laid in the dust; but there is a crown of glory reserved for Christ's spiritual seed, which fadeth not away. From all this complaint learn what work sin makes with families, noble families, with families in which religion has appeared. They plead with God for mercy. God's unchangeableness and faithfulness assure us that He will not cast off those whom he has chosen and covenanted with. They were reproached for serving him. The scoffers of the latter days, in like manner, reproach the footsteps of the Messiah when they ask, Where is the promise of his coming? 2Pe 3:3, 4. The records of the Lord's dealings with the family of David, show us his dealings with his church, and with believers. Their afflictions and distresses may be grievous, but he will not finally cast them off. Self-deceivers abuse this doctrine, and others by a careless walk bring themselves into darkness and distress; yet let the true believer rely on it for encouragement in the path of duty, and in bearing the cross. The psalm ends with praise, even after this sad complaint. Those who give God thanks for what he has done, may give him thanks for what he will do. God will follow those with his mercies, who follow him with praises.
